Subject: Proposed DPA changes - training/data use + subprocessors

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited about the latency numbers and the integration path. Our legal team has a few narrow asks on the DPA we need to resolve before we move forward:

1) Training & model use: we need an explicit prohibition on using our customer data to improve base models or to train any shared models. We understand redwood has telemetry and caching; we want to ensure PHI/PII is never used for training.
2) Subprocessors: we need the subprocessors list limited to our cloud provider (GCP) and a named analytics vendor. No other third parties without prior written consent.
3) Audit/retention: small tweaks to retention windows and on-demand audit evidence for our SOC team.

Attached is our proposed redline (nimbus_proposed_redline_v1.pdf). Can you share Redwood's position and an estimated timeline for sign-off? We are aiming to finalize contracts by mid-December.

Regards,
Jake Fuller
Director, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Nimbus Health

Jake / team — quick Product note on feasibility and impact.

Summary position (product):
- We can agree to a contract-level prohibition on using Nimbus customer content to train our shared public models. However, to maintain service functionality there are two pragmatic options we prefer to offer:
  a) Pseudonymization carveout: Redwood will not use any raw PII/PHI for model training; we will implement a pseudonymization pipeline for customer logs used for aggregate quality monitoring. Pseudonymization removes direct identifiers before any downstream modeling.
  b) Opt-out + dedicated telemetry: For full training opt-out, we can also offer a Dedicated/Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) where telemetry is tightly scoped, but this changes commercial terms (reserved capacity).

Technical impact and timeline:
- Implementing the pseudonymization and configuration flag to exclude Nimbus traffic from training pipelines: ~3 weeks (QA + staging).
- Disabling automated telemetry export for the account and enabling a scoped telemetry retention policy: 1 week.
- If Nimbus requires guaranteed GCP-region-only residency for all artifacts, that will require a short infra change and could add 2-3 weeks depending on region availability.

Subprocessors: from Product perspective, we can support a subprocessors carveout that lists only GCP and the named analytics vendor. We’ll need Legal to manage the contractual notification mechanism (e.g., 30 days prior notice + consent for new subprocessors).

I’m attaching a short data flow diagram that shows where pseudonymization would occur in our pipeline. Evelyn — please confirm security acceptability on pseudonymization approach and audit log availability. Olga — appreciate suggested contract language we can use.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Jake — thanks for the clear redline. We reviewed and propose the following negotiation positions (high-level):

1) Training prohibition: Redwood can accept an explicit prohibition on using Nimbus-provided customer content to train Redwood’s public or shared models. We propose the following counter-language: "Redwood shall not use Customer Content to train or retrain any models that are part of Redwood's publicly-available model catalog. Redwood may use aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry for internal service quality monitoring and infrastructure optimization, provided such telemetry contains no direct identifiers and cannot be reconstituted to identify Customer or End Users."

2) Subprocessors: agreed to limit to GCP + named vendor in schedule. We request a standard "notification and consent" process: Redwood will notify Customer 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor; Customer may object in writing and the parties will negotiate in good faith. If Customer's objection is reasonable and material, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide alternatives (e.g., dedicated deployment).

3) Audit & retention: propose a committed retention window (90 days for raw request logs, 365 days for aggregated metrics) and scope of evidence for audits (SSE, SOC-2 reports, access logs). For one-off audit requests we can provide scoped export with appropriate NDAs and cost-recovery if significant.

Next steps: I will assemble a redlined DPA reflecting the above and circulate internally — Marissa, can you confirm whether Nimbus will accept the pseudonymization compromise or insist on a full training ban with no telemetry? Evelyn, please confirm whether the pseudonymization approach satisfies security for PHI/PII controls and whether additional encryption/HSM controls are required.

Warmly,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
